title: Epidemic growth and the reproduction number
summary: Exponential growth rate r of influenza seasons, converted to R, and the SIR model's herd-immunity threshold and final size.

concepts.label: Influenza season
concepts.description: Epiweek 40 to 39 of the next year, US national.

children.label: Influenza-like illness (ILI)
children.description: Share of outpatient visits with fever and cough or sore throat (wILI, %).

children.label: Test positivity
children.description: Share of clinical-lab specimens positive for influenza.

children.label: ILI+
children.description: ILI × positivity: a proxy for influenza incidence.

facts.text: ILI × % positive as a proxy for influenza incidence: Goldstein et al. 2011.

children.label: Influenza subtype
children.description: A(H3N2), A(H1N1)pdm09, B: only A and B totals are here.

concepts.label: SIR model
concepts.description: Susceptible–infected–recovered compartments in a well-mixed population.

children.label: Growth rate r
children.description: Exponential growth per week in the early epidemic.

children.label: Reproduction number R
children.description: Infections caused per infection; from r and the generation interval.

facts.text: R from r and the generation-interval distribution: Wallinga & Lipsitch 2007.

children.label: Herd-immunity threshold
children.description: 1 − 1/R: the immune share at which growth stops.

concepts.label: Generation interval
concepts.description: Time from one infection to the next it causes (3 days assumed).

concepts.label: Population immunity
concepts.description: Vaccination and earlier infections: why effective R is below R0.
